A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPA research despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BBH adaptation analyses, commonsense reasoning and VTAB-1k accuracy results, and projector ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, projection and compute controls, and a feature-similarity analysis.

M1.justification: The reconstruction objective, tied linear encoder/decoder, default IPCA pretraining, and optional projector fine-tuning remain unchanged. The reconstructive terminology and additional comparison methods do not change IPA's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 27 BBH tasks, commonsense-170k with eight reasoning benchmarks, and 19 VTAB-1k tasks. The new analyses use this retained coverage without introducing another domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the Llama-3 comparison beyond LoRA and DoRA by evaluating PiSSA, OLoRA, CorDA, RandLoRA, and VeRA (Tables 3 and 6). Tables 4 and 7 additionally evaluate random-orthogonal projection comparators under two scaling configurations.

E3.justification: New protocols include orthogonal-projection scaling controls, BBH feature-space cosine evaluation, and an approximately matched-time comparison using 32,887 LoRA steps versus 31,926 IPA steps (Table 10). The original benchmark splits, training schedules, and accuracy evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial checks of whether IPA's advantage comes from orthogonality or additional compute, plus comparative resource measurements. Appendix B and Figure 5 also test whether weight similarity implies similarity of projected features. The original algorithm, rank, and pretraining-subset ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports paired, two-sided sign tests comparing IPA with LoRA and DoRA across the 19 VTAB tasks, separately for each projector setting. Existing seed disclosures remain; no repeated-training uncertainty estimates or confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: The main accuracy tables and original ablation scores are unchanged, but v2 substantially extends the results. Examples include PiSSA's 84.6 versus IPA's 85.9 in the added Llama-3 comparison, and extended-budget LoRA's 85.0 versus IPA's 85.9 in Table 10. New orthogonal-projection, resource, significance, and feature-similarity findings are also reported.

T1.justification: The LoRA equations, reconstruction objective, and PCA characterization are retained without new proofs or substantive derivations. The identity-projector observation and standard cosine formula for the new feature analysis provide explanation and evaluation detail rather than new theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution qualify the information-preservation framing: 'explicitly preserves' and 'maximizes information preservation' become aiming to reconstruct inputs and favoring reconstruction. The headline accuracy improvements and roughly half-parameter claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking identity projection to full fine-tuning, motivating norm compensation, and interpreting the compute-budget control. Appendix B describes moderate projected-feature similarity. The new assertion that orthogonal projections consistently underperform LoRA is overstated: Table 4 includes an 85.5 tie.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link, learning rates for additional baselines, exact step counts for the compute control, and comparative runtime and peak-memory information. Appendix A's existing hyperparameters are retained; H100 hardware and IPA pretraining times were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Hotelling's PCA work and Büyükakyüz's OLoRA, and discusses the expanded comparison across random-projection and decomposition methods. The existing related-work section and input-feature-based positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and reconstruction terminology, adds short explanations, inserts the extended-comparison Section 4.3, and moves ablations to Section 4.4. Appendix B expands and Appendix A's heading is simplified, while most existing prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through new comparator, projection-control, and compute-budget tables and Figure 5. Figure 1's initialization strip becomes horizontal, Table 2 gains a significance column, and projector-setting cells are regrouped. Existing figures and ablation tables are retained with relocation, renumbering, and some row reordering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's empirical support by testing broader PEFT alternatives and controlling for orthogonality and extra pretraining compute, with detailed appendix results. Feature-space diagnostics and VTAB sign tests further strengthen scrutiny of the central argument. The added baseline experiments remain concentrated on Llama-3 and one comparison passage overstates a tie, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in validation.
